classifications.label: Instrumental: four independent measurement systems with uncorrelated noise and independent calibration drift
Environmental: a shared external driver (temperature, vibration, or electromagnetic) modulates all four streams with different coupling strengths and/or delays
Measurement protocol artifact: observer bias, recording error, or systematic misalignment of trial numbering between lab and observatory instruments

Methodological: I have not yet collected enough post-baseline data to detect true instrumental drift or periodic behavior; the 10-day baseline is too short to establish reliable autocorrelation structure
Trial numbering or index misalignment between lab and observatory instruments
Independent instrumental noise and calibration drift (no systematic environmental coupling)
Shared environmental driver (temperature, vibration, or electromagnetic) with different coupling strengths and instrumental transmission delays
Insufficient post-baseline data; current anomalies are statistical artifacts from multiple comparisons and small sample sizes

Systematic error in my autocorrelation analysis: lag misspecification or accidental row-shifting during resampling

Trial sequence misalignment in my digital transcription between field notebooks and lab/observatory records, concentrated in the pendulum_obs and resonator_obs logs around Days 10–15.
Systematic bug in my lag-computation code: off-by-one error or row-shift during resampling that introduces spurious negative autocorrelations.

Weak shared environmental driver (e.g., 10–14 day thermal or vibration cycle from settlement infrastructure) coupling to all instruments with differential phase lags and/or instrument-specific coupling strengths, masked by instrumental noise.

Post-baseline miscalibration or re-zeroing of observatory instruments (pendulum_obs and/or resonator_obs) on Days 10–15, accompanied by a trial-numbering reset or data-entry protocol change that introduced a persistent index offset in the digital record.

False positives from multiple comparisons: current anomalies are real correlations but of physical origin too weak to trust at current sample size (n ∼ 36–96 pairs per lag); continuing to Day 25–30 will separate signal from noise.
